plan: dispatch://INFRA-721/artifact/plan-md (v1). The plan is three changes to the Dispatch ask-edit route in one pull request against sjawhar/legion, all production code under packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs/: (1) an options edit pairs each option it sends with the list item already in the document, by label with the first unused match, reuses an unchanged option's node whole, rewrites only the first paragraph of a changed option and keeps the rest of its item, and refuses, quoting the content and naming dispatch doc-edit, an edit that would drop an item holding more than its plain line (a removal, a rename, --clear-options); (2) SetAskBlockText reads a block whose one parse failure is an empty question leniently, applies the edit on that reading when the edit carries a non-empty question, and otherwise refuses with the step that applies, while refuseAskContentEdit/planAskRepair name, for a broken ask with no paragraph holding text, one document edit that deletes the extra blocks and writes the question before the list it keeps; (3) the four round-12 points of sjawhar/legion#2433, among them askRepairDrops naming a nested decision's own node where deleting its children would leave it holding nothing. Ten acceptance criteria, each with its surface and its command, are in the plan's Acceptance part.

implement: legion-worker: the implementer works a shared jj workspace, pushes the issue branch itself, opens the pull request with the Dispatch line and ends the phase with handoff_complete; its references/pr-body.md defines the six-field proof entry every acceptance criterion needs, references/tools.md puts every tool install on the issue volume under $TMPDIR (this pod has no Postgres and no Docker, and the plan's T1 builds one), references/findings.md keeps a defect in a file this change touches inside this pull request, and references/skip-checks-trailer.md keeps the trailer off a code push
ce-simplify-code: the options-pairing helpers and the repair planner are new, settled code in ask_block_text.go, and the simplify pass over them runs before the phase completes
dispatch, dispatch-first: every Dispatch read or write in this phase, and the search before any finding is reported
asd-ste100: the pull-request body and every message this phase sends
test: legion-worker: the tester re-runs the commands the plan's Acceptance part names and records its own proof entries; references/pr-body.md defines what a proof and its negative control are, and references/tools.md covers the Postgres and the Dispatch harness it needs on the issue volume, including the rule never to stop the server a sibling role left running
dispatch, asd-ste100: the tester's report and any message to the architect
review: legion-worker: references/merge-gate.md gives the reviewer's four GitHub reads, the approval of the head by SHA and what may sit above it, references/review-threads.md how threads are answered and resolved, and references/pr-body.md how a proof is judged and which prose findings the reviewer fixes itself
asd-ste100: the review body and every thread reply

findings.finding: The Change makes preservation mandatory for an option the edit does not change, but an options edit carries no identity for an option, so nothing says how a sent option pairs with a list item already in the document (rename, reorder, removal, a new option, duplicate labels), nor what an edit that shortens the list or sends --clear-options does with the content under the options it drops.
findings.answer: Design D1 and the decision 'Pair a sent option with a document item by label, not by position': by label, first unused match, which is stable under reordering and is a function when a document holds two items with one label; a sent option no item matches is a new item; an item no sent option matches is dropped only when it holds nothing but its plain line, and otherwise the whole edit is refused with that item's markdown quoted and dispatch doc-edit named. That one rule covers removal, rename and --clear-options.

findings.finding: The spec's empty-question remedy cannot repair the state the tester found, which is empty-question and a second bullet list at once: an edit-ask carrying a question still meets refuseAskContentEdit, and a doc-edit of deletes alone is refused because the post-edit node still has an empty question.
findings.answer: Design D3. planAskRepair models the one document edit as deletes plus the question the same edit writes: where no paragraph of the edited ask holds text, the drop set keeps the run of paragraphs from the start and the first bullet list after them, the holder and changed re-reads are done against a tree carrying that question paragraph, and the refusal names the deletes and the step that writes the question before the list it keeps. No gate is relaxed: ApplyOps validates once, on the final tree. Acceptance A6 follows that path to a valid ask and asserts every word of the blocks the refusal did not name is still there.

findings.finding: Three claims of the empty-question paragraph are unsupported: that every doc-edit touching the ask is refused, that an agent has no path at all, and that every agent edit of it is refused with that sentence (a decided ask, an approval ask and another session's ask are refused earlier in api/asks.go with other codes).
findings.answer: Recorded in the plan's 'What is wrong today' as a correction, and in specDepartures: refuseChangedAsks judges the ask as the edit leaves it, so a doc-edit that writes a question back is accepted today and one path does exist; what is missing is that no refusal names it. D2's last paragraph records that a decided or resolved ask (409 ASK_NOT_OPEN), an approval ask (409 ASK_KIND_FIXED) and a non-author session (403 NOT_AUTHOR) are refused before the document is read and need no path, since settlement writes a decided ask's wording back once its body is repaired.

findings.finding: A1's 'byte for byte' names no representation; read as 'the rendered markdown is unchanged' it is satisfied by an implementation that re-parses the whole list and mints fresh block ids, orphaning a comment anchored inside the preserved sub-list.
findings.answer: Acceptance A1 states the checkable form: the untouched list_item after the edit equals the node before it under pmdoc.Node.EqualWithBlockIDs, so the block ids, the marks and the link's address are the same node and not an equal rendering. T3 adds the anchored-comment assertion, and D1 says the original block ids are written back onto the parsed items.

findings.finding: Preserving nodes meets invariants the spec does not mention: the list's spread attribute when a preserved spread item is spliced into a parser-built list, the write budget the merged list is parsed on, and the ': '-in-a-label refusal that compares the block's re-parse with the caller's values.
findings.answer: D1's 'How the nodes are built' and 'Invariants this must not break': the merged list is rendered and parsed back whole so the parser decides spread over the merged markdown, then the original block ids and child nodes are restored; compareAskBlockText still holds because a reused item parses back to the pair it was matched on; and the budget is the plan's one recorded Unsure, which T2 measures with a large preserved sub-list before the choice is made. The spread risk is in the Risks list with T3's fingerprint assertion.

findings.finding: The three-level refusal fix would name a delete that refuseRemovingOpenDecisionBlocks in the CLI throws on, because that guard refuses a delete of an ask block with an open ask row and of any block containing one.
findings.answer: D3's last paragraph: a decision that never had a question never had a row, since addedAskBlocks and readableAskBlockIDs skip a block the parser refuses, so the common case passes the guard; the refusal carries one clause for the case where a person emptied a decision that had a row, saying it is answered or resolved first or repaired in the editor. T6 checks the premise and the Risks list says what to do if it is false.

findings.finding: Giving an empty-question ask a repair path forces work in the 1,364-body corpus: noDeleteExplanation accepts the empty-question sentence as a legitimate end, and followAskRefusal can only send an urgency edit, so it cannot follow a repair that needs a question.
findings.answer: Design D4 and task T7, named as the bulk of the test work, with acceptance A8 running both exhaustive tests. The corpus's probing edit stays AskBlockEdit{Urgency}, because D2 makes that refusal itself name the deletes and the question step; followAskRefusal gains an insert of a question paragraph in the same ApplyOps call and sends that question with the ask edit, and noDeleteExplanation stops excusing an empty question.

findings.finding: A3 names no command, no document and no expected output, 'every word kept' cannot see a loss with no words (an image, a link whose text is empty), and no criterion at all covers the refusal wording for an edit-ask --urgency on an empty-question ask, which is the tester's actual complaint.
findings.answer: A3 now names the harness, the three commands, the expected content of the doc-read output and a negative control against a server built from 2b427f93. The no-word loss is closed in D2: the lenient path refuses, quoting the block, when a paragraph it would replace holds anything but plain text and hard breaks. A5 is the new criterion for the refusal wording of an edit that carries no question.

findings.finding: askBlockChildren has a second caller the spec never mentions: writeDecidedWording, which settlement uses to write a decided ask's recorded wording back into its block, so any option preservation changes that path too.
findings.answer: D1's last paragraph records it as intended behaviour (the restore keeps a sub-list a person wrote under an option after the decision, where today it flattens it), and T3 pins it with a test on that path, where docs/approval_carry_test.go already sits.

findings.finding: The spec's paraphrase of the third review item ('the empty-question drop in blocksTheAskRuleLeavesNoRoomFor') is narrower than the review's rule ('drop a decision's own blocks only when its own block types break the rule'); fixing only the empty-paragraph branch leaves the item unfixed. Documentation and a changelog fragment are unstated work.
findings.answer: Task T8 states the review's rule: gate the helper's own-block drops on the decision's own child types, as askBreaksItsOwnRule does, and always recurse into nested decisions. Task T9 covers packages/envoy/AGENTS.md's ask-edit paragraph and the paragraph on an unreadable block, and one changie fragment per package changed, named for the pull request.

specDepartures.spec: The issue states, of an ask whose question a person emptied, that 'every doc-edit that touches it is refused with ask block "<id>" has an empty question' and that 'an agent then has no path to repair it, on main and after #2433 alike'.
specDepartures.plan: The plan records that a document edit which writes a question back into the block is accepted today, so one path exists, and that what is missing is that no refusal names it. It still builds the issue's remedy (an edit-ask carrying a question repairs the block) and adds that every refusal on this route names a step.
specDepartures.evidence: refuseChangedAsks in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs/ask_blocks.go judges each ask as the edit leaves it and returns nil as soon as the post-edit node parses, so only an edit that touches the block and leaves the question empty is refused. The tester's report was of an ask that was empty-question and held two lists, where both refusals do fire.

specDepartures.spec: The Change paragraph makes preservation mandatory for an option the edit does not change and leaves the implementer to keep or refuse for an option it changes. It says nothing about an option the edit removes or renames.
specDepartures.plan: The plan keeps the content for an option the edit rewrites, and refuses the whole edit, quoting the content and naming dispatch doc-edit, when an item that holds more than its plain line matches no option the edit sends: a removal, a rename, or --clear-options.
specDepartures.evidence: Those three edits delete a person's sub-list, second paragraph, link or marks exactly as the edit the issue reports does, and the agent cannot see the content either (dispatch read --ask prints the row's label and description only, askSummary in packages/envoy-client/src/dispatch-execute.ts). Dropping it silently would leave the defect open on three of the four shapes of an options edit.
